title: the web shell discards every daemon refusal because it reads a field the daemon does not send
body:
The shell page's client detects daemon refusals by reading `answer.body.error`.
The daemon never sends a field by that name, so NO refusal is ever detected:
the page falls through to the success path and renders an empty form while
the daemon's message and remedy are discarded.

MINE. Landed in 326dbc1f with the browse work. Found while driving `Op::Form`
through the DELIVERED pair (92e4d914a) on vc's instruction -- the drive was
about something else and this fell out of the negative control, which is the
argument for running controls at all.

DRIVEN, against the running daemon, delivered pair 92e4d914a:

    POST /op {"root":"...","op":"form","view":"/thread/ST9999"}
    -> http 200
    {"result":"error","message":"no steel thread ST9999 in this project",
     "remedy":"run `intent st list` to see the threads this project has"}

`wire::Response` is `#[serde(tag = "result", rename_all = "snake_case")]`, so
a refusal is `result: "error"` with the text in `message`. There is no `error`
KEY anywhere in the payload. `answer.body.error` is therefore `undefined` for
every refusal the daemon can produce.

WHAT THE READER SEES, from source (`renderForm`), not from a browser:
`form.entity` and `form.title` are both undefined, so the breadcrumb renders
"intentd / undefined", the `<h1>` renders "undefined", and `(form.fields ||
[])` iterates nothing. A precise, well-authored refusal becomes a blank page
that looks like a broken form.

THE COMMENT DIRECTLY ABOVE THE BUG STATES THE CORRECT RULE: "The daemon
reports its own refusals INSIDE a well-formed response, so a 200 is not on
its own a success and the body is what decides." The reasoning was right and
the field name was wrong, so the guard is PRESENT and aimed at a noun that
does not exist -- the same class as the misaimed `st_show` in 0238, and
invisible to any search for a missing check.

THE `status !== 200` ARM DOES NOT COVER IT and cannot: the daemon
deliberately answers refusals at 200 with the fault inside the body, which is
what the comment is about. So the one branch that could catch this is the one
that is broken.

THE FIX IS ONE PREDICATE -- key on `result === "error"` and read `message`.
It is NOT written yet: filed before fixing, per vc's standing file-then-fix.

WHY NO TEST CAUGHT IT: the web-face tests assert what the DAEMON sends and
the deep-link test asserts the shell is SERVED. Nothing executes the page's
JavaScript, so the client's own branch logic is untested by construction.
Worth saying explicitly rather than leaving as an absence -- whether that
gets a harness is a bigger question than this fix.

RELATED: 0238 (the terminal half of the same "nothing checks existence"
family, now fixed) and 0240 (its unfixed siblings). `intent browse` no longer
composes a URL for a missing entity, so the common route into this state is
closed -- but a bookmark, a reload, or a hand-typed deep link still reaches
it, which is exactly what the deep-link fallback exists to serve.
